q: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence: "Water ________ at 100 degrees Celsius under standard atmospheric pressure."
e: Universal scientific truths and natural laws are always expressed in the Simple Present (Present Indefinite) tense. "Is boiling" denotes a temporary ongoing action, while "has boiled" and "boiled" denote completed past events.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate tense form: "She ________ for this university since 2018."
e: Actions that began at a definite point in the past ("since 2018") and continue into the present require the Present Perfect Continuous tense ("has been working"). Simple Continuous ("is working") cannot take "since + point of time".

q: Select the correct verb form: "The delegates ________ for Lucknow yesterday evening."
e: Definite past time adverbs such as "yesterday", "last night", and "ago" strictly require the Simple Past tense ("left"). Present Perfect ("have left") cannot be used with a finished past time marker.

q: Complete the sentence: "While I ________ my essay, the lights suddenly went out."
e: When a shorter past action ("went out") interrupts a longer background action in progress, the longer action takes the Past Continuous ("was writing") and the interrupting action takes the Simple Past.

q: Fill in the blank: "By the end of next month, the engineers ________ the new bridge."
e: Time expressions beginning with "By + future time" ("By the end of next month") indicate completion prior to a future deadline and therefore require the Future Perfect tense ("will have completed").

q: Choose the grammatically correct option: "If it ________ tomorrow, the inter-college match will be postponed."
e: In a Type 1 (Open/Probable) Conditional sentence, the subordinate 'if'-clause uses the Simple Present ("rains") while the main clause uses Simple Future ("will be postponed"). Using "will" in the 'if'-clause is incorrect.

q: Choose the correct verb: "Bread and butter ________ his staple breakfast every morning."
e: When two singular nouns joined by "and" express a single unified idea or dish ("bread and butter", "slow and steady"), they take a singular verb ("is").

q: Select the correct verb form: "Each of the shortlisted candidates ________ been invited for an interview."
e: Distributive pronouns like "each", "everyone", "either", and "neither" are grammatically singular and always take a singular verb ("has"), regardless of the plural noun ("candidates") following "of".

q: Fill in the blank: "Neither the teacher nor the students ________ aware of the sudden schedule change."
e: Under the Rule of Proximity, when subjects of different numbers are joined by "either...or" or "neither...nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject ("students" — plural), requiring "were".

q: Complete the sentence correctly: "The principal, as well as the faculty members, ________ attending the seminar."
e: When two subjects are linked by "as well as", "along with", "together with", or "in addition to", the verb agrees strictly with the first subject ("The principal" — singular), so "is" is correct.

q: Choose the correct option: "He told me that he ________ his assignment before dinner."
e: By the Sequence of Tenses, a past reporting verb ("told") shifts the subordinate clause into a corresponding past tense; an action completed prior to another past reference takes the Past Perfect ("had finished").

q: Fill in the blank with the correct pronoun: "One must always keep ________ promises."
e: When the indefinite pronoun "one" is used as the subject in a general sense, its possessive form throughout the sentence must be "one's" (not "his" or "their").

q: Select the correct verb: "Mathematics ________ considered the queen of all sciences."
e: Names of academic disciplines ending in '-ics' (Mathematics, Physics, Economics, Civics) are singular in meaning when referring to the subject itself and take a singular verb ("is").

q: Complete the sentence: "If I ________ a bird, I would fly across the Himalayas."
e: In an unreal/hypothetical present conditional (Type 2), the past subjunctive "were" is used for all persons (including "I", "he", "she") in formal standard English.

q: Choose the correct verb form: "I ________ never ________ such a gripping historical novel before."
e: Life experiences up to the present moment accompanied by adverbs like "never", "ever", or "before" take the Present Perfect tense ("have read").

q: Choose the correct verb forms: "The train ________ the platform before we ________ the station."
e: When two actions occurred in the past, the earlier completed action takes the Past Perfect ("had left") and the subsequent action takes the Simple Past ("reached").

q: Identify the grammatically CORRECT sentence among the following:
o: This mango is tasting remarkably sweet.
She is knowing the answer to this riddle.
They are resembling their maternal grandfather.
e: Stative verbs of possession, perception, and cognition ("know", "own", "resemble", "taste" in stative sense) are not normally used in continuous tenses. Only "He owns three antique manuscripts" uses the stative verb correctly.

q: Fill in the blank: "If you had informed me earlier, I ________ the tickets in advance."
e: Type 3 (Unfulfilled Past) Conditionals follow the structure: If + Past Perfect ("had informed"), Subject + would/could/might + have + V₃ ("would have booked").

q: Choose the correct completion: "Galileo proved that the Earth ________ around the Sun."
e: As a key exception to the Sequence of Tenses, when a subordinate clause states a universal truth, scientific law, or habitual fact, it remains in the Simple Present ("revolves") even after a past reporting verb ("proved").

q: Select the correct verb: "The jury ________ divided in their opinions regarding the verdict."
e: A collective noun ("jury", "committee", "audience") takes a singular verb when acting as one unified body, but a plural verb ("were") when its individual members act separately or disagree ("divided in their opinions").

q: Choose the correct pair of verbs: "A large number of applicants ________ arrived, yet the number of vacancies ________ strictly limited."
e: "A number of + plural noun" means "many" and takes a plural verb ("have"), whereas "The number of + plural noun" refers to a single numerical figure and takes a singular verb ("is").

q: Fill in the blank: "Many a brave soldier ________ laid down his life for the motherland."
e: The idiomatic determiner "Many a + singular countable noun" is plural in sense but strictly singular in grammatical form, requiring both a singular verb ("has") and singular pronoun ("his").

q: Complete the sentence: "Fifty kilometres ________ a long distance to walk in a single day."
e: Plural expressions denoting a fixed sum of money, period of time, weight, or distance considered as a single unit ("Fifty kilometres") always take a singular verb ("is").

q: Choose the correct verb form: "It is high time you ________ preparing seriously for the examination."
e: Expressions like "It is time", "It is high time", and "It is about time" followed by a subject take the Simple Past (unreal past subjunctive) form ("started") to imply urgency.

q: Fill in the blank: "Walk carefully lest you ________ on the wet marble floor."
e: The negative conjunction "lest" (meaning "for fear that") is always followed by the modal auxiliary "should" (or bare subjunctive in formal American usage), never "may", "will", or "not".

q: Choose the correct verb: "She is one of those rare scholars who ________ never satisfied with superficial answers."
e: In the construction "one of + plural noun + who/that", the antecedent of the relative pronoun "who" is the plural noun ("rare scholars"), so the verb in the relative clause must be plural ("are").

q: Select the correct pronoun: "Neither the captain nor the players neglected ________ duties."
e: When singular and plural antecedents are joined by "neither...nor", the possessive pronoun agrees with the nearer antecedent ("players" — plural), requiring "their".

q: Choose the most idiomatic verb form: "The Shatabdi Express ________ New Delhi at 6:00 a.m. sharp tomorrow."
e: Fixed timetables, official itineraries, and scheduled public transport departures in the future are idiomatically expressed in the Simple Present tense ("leaves").

q: Complete the sentence accurately: "Ten years ________ since we last met at Prayagraj."
e: The standard tense pattern with conjunction "since" is: Present Perfect ("have passed") in the main clause + "since" + Simple Past ("last met") in the subordinate clause.

q: Choose the correct verb: "The poet and philosopher ________ invited to deliver the convocation address."
e: When two nouns joined by "and" share a SINGLE article before the first noun ("The poet and philosopher"), they refer to one and the same person, taking a singular verb ("was"). (Repeating "the" — "The poet and the philosopher" — would require "were".)

q: Fill in the blank: "________ I known about your illness, I would have visited you immediately."
e: In formal Type 3 Conditionals, "If" can be omitted by inverting the auxiliary "Had" before the subject ("Had I known..." = "If I had known...").

q: Complete the sentence: "Two-thirds of the city ________ in ruins after the earthquake, and two-thirds of the residents ________ displaced."
e: With fractions and percentages ("two-thirds of", "half of"), the verb agrees with the noun inside the 'of'-phrase: singular uncountable/singular noun ("city") takes "was", while plural countable noun ("residents") takes "were".

q: Choose the correct option: "She liked you much better than she ________ me today."
e: Another key exception to the Sequence of Tenses: a clause of comparison introduced by "than" or "as" can take ANY tense required by the sense—here "today" requires Simple Present ("likes").

q: Select the correct verb form: "He orders everyone around as though he ________ the sole proprietor of the firm."
e: After "as if" and "as though" expressing a contrary-to-fact present supposition, the past subjunctive "were" is required for all subjects.

q: Identify the grammatically correct sentence for a positive/neutral statement:
o: I, you and he will represent the department at the conference.
You, he and I will represent the department at the conference.
He, I and you will represent the department at the conference.
You, I and he will represent the department at the conference.
e: For singular personal pronouns in a pleasant/neutral context, standard English follows the 2-3-1 sequence (Second person "You" → Third person "he" → First person "I"). (For admitting guilt/fault or with plural pronouns, the 1-2-3 order is used.)

q: Choose the correct verb form for this Mixed Conditional: "If he had invested wisely in his youth, he ________ struggling to pay his bills today."
e: A Mixed Conditional links a counterfactual past condition ("had invested" — Type 3) to a counterfactual PRESENT result ("today"), requiring "would + base verb / would be + V-ing" ("would not be struggling").

q: Select the grammatically accurate formal sentence using the mandative subjunctive:
o: The committee recommended that every candidate submits his dossier by Friday.
The committee recommended that every candidate submit his dossier by Friday.
The committee recommended that every candidate submitted his dossier by Friday.
The committee recommended that every candidate has submitted his dossier by Friday.
e: Verbs of demand, suggestion, or recommendation ("recommend", "insist", "demand", "propose", "suggest") followed by a 'that'-clause require the bare infinitive (present subjunctive) without '-s' ("submit") in formal standard English.

q: Choose the correct verb: "Dr. Sen is the only one of our professors who ________ published five monographs on Shakespeare."
e: Unlike "one of those professors who + plural verb", the restrictive phrase "the ONLY one of + plural noun + who" shifts the antecedent of "who" strictly to the singular "the only one", requiring the singular verb "has".

q: Fill in the blanks accurately: "More than one manuscript ________ missing, while more students than one ________ protested the decision."
e: "More than one + singular noun" takes a singular verb ("is"), whereas the split construction "More + plural noun + than one" takes a plural verb ("have").

q: Choose the correct option to complete the inverted conditional: "________ to resign tomorrow, the board would face an immediate leadership vacuum."
e: Formal Type 2 Conditional inversion uses "Were + subject + to-infinitive" ("Were the director to resign..." = "If the director were to resign..."). "Was" cannot be used in subjunctive inversion.

q: Select the correct verb form: "Nothing but charred ruins ________ visible after the devastating fire."
e: In "Nothing but + noun", the true grammatical subject is the singular indefinite pronoun "Nothing" ("but charred ruins" is a prepositional phrase), so the verb is always singular ("was").

q: Choose the most precise option: "By the time the rescue helicopter arrived, the mountaineers ________ in sub-zero winds for fourteen hours."
e: An action that began earlier in the past and continued uninterruptedly up to another past point ("By the time...arrived") with a stated duration ("for fourteen hours") demands the Past Perfect Continuous ("had been waiting").

q: Choose the correct verb: "What the students urgently need right now ________ clear guidance and regular mock tests."
e: When a nominal 'what'-clause serves as subject and is followed by a plural complement ("clear guidance and regular mock tests"), standard usage prefers a plural verb ("are") to agree with the plural complement.

q: Identify the grammatically flawless sentence:
o: Hardly had the lecture begun than the microphone failed.
Hardly the lecture had begun when the microphone failed.
Hardly had the lecture begun when the microphone failed.
Hardly did the lecture begun when the microphone failed.
e: Negative adverbs "Hardly" and "Scarcely" placed at the start of a sentence trigger subject-auxiliary inversion ("Hardly had the lecture begun") and pair strictly with "when" (never "than", which pairs with "No sooner").

q: Select the correct pair of verbs: "The scissors ________ blunt, and all the luggage ________ been loaded onto the van."
e: Paired-part tools ("scissors", "trousers", "spectacles") without "a pair of" are always plural ("are"), whereas uncountable collective nouns ("luggage", "furniture", "scenery", "machinery") are always singular ("has").

q: Choose the correct verb form expressing regret about a past event: "I wish I ________ more attention to classical prosody during my graduation."
e: "Wish + Simple Past" expresses present regret ("I wish I knew"), whereas "Wish + Past Perfect" ("had paid") expresses regret over an unchangeable past action.

q: Choose the correct verb: "His politics ________ markedly more conservative than those of his elder brother."
e: When '-ics' nouns like "politics", "statistics", or "economics" are preceded by a possessive determiner ("His politics" = political views; "The statistics" = numerical data), they become plural in sense and take a plural verb ("are").

q: Fill in the blank: "Next June, Professor Verma ________ English literature at Allahabad University for thirty years."
e: To indicate an action continuing up to and across a specified future benchmark ("Next June") with an explicit duration ("for thirty years"), the Future Perfect Continuous ("will have been teaching") is required.

q: Identify the sentence with ZERO agreement errors:
o: Every boy and every girl must submit their admit card before entering.
Each of the two sisters forgot to bring their identity proof.
Either of the proposals has its own practical merits.
Neither of the two witnesses remembered their exact statement.
e: "Either" is strictly singular and correctly takes both the singular verb "has" and singular possessive "its". In A, B, and D, "Every", "Each", and "Neither" are singular antecedents paired incorrectly with plural "their" in formal exam grammar.

q: Choose the correct completion: "But for your timely intervention, the entire negotiation ________."
e: The prepositional phrase "But for + noun phrase" acts as an implied Type 3 conditional ("If it had not been for your timely intervention..."), requiring the conditional perfect ("would have collapsed") in the main clause.
